item.title: EU INC | 2026-W11
item.description:
eu-inc Weekly | 2026-W11

No new items surfaced in the delta analysis this week; the queue reflects recirculated background on the 28th regime and adjacent capital-market moves rather than fresh developments.

This Week

28th regime - Wikipedia (Wikipedia) -- The most comprehensive public summary of the EU Inc legislative timeline, including the July 2025 Commission proposal and current Council progress.

En qué consiste EU Inc (Diario Tecnología) -- Spanish-language explainer covering the structural gaps -- fragmented incorporation rules, thin exit markets -- that EU Inc is designed to close.

European Commission launches consultation on private equity exits (Global Regulation Tomorrow) -- The Commission is actively consulting on improving PE exit pathways, a parallel track to EU Inc that directly affects late-stage startup liquidity.

EU firms coping well with US tariffs, face obstacles within bloc, EIB survey shows (Reuters) -- EIB survey data quantifying internal single-market fragmentation -- the exact problem EU Inc's 28th regime is meant to reduce for company formation and cross-border scaling.

What's In The EU Buy-European Law? (World Energy News) -- The Industrial Accelerator Act uses public procurement preferences to anchor demand for EU-made goods, providing complementary industrial policy context for the startup-formation push.

item.title: EU INC | 2026-W10
item.description:
eu-inc Weekly | 2026-W10

A quiet week on the EU Inc front -- no major legislative moves, but the analytical layer thickened as law firms and business press caught up to the January Davos moment.

This Week

EU Inc. -- The Truly European Company Structure (McDermott Will & Emery) -- A major international law firm publishes its first detailed client briefing on EU Inc., framing von der Leyen's January 20 Davos announcement as a historic turning point.

EU Inc. May Solve Legal Issues, But Scaling Across Borders Still Depends on How Teams Work (European Business Review) -- Argues that legal harmonization is necessary but not sufficient, as operational and HR complexity across member states persists regardless of corporate structure.

Startups fordern Verordnung zur EU Inc (Börsen-Zeitung) -- German startup community pushes specifically for a regulation (directly applicable) rather than a directive, and flags capital gains tax triggers when founders relocate between EU countries.

What is EU-INC and its plan to make European businesses borderless? (Euronews) -- Clean explainer piece useful for briefing newcomers to the topic.

New Arguments

  • ❌ A unified corporate form does not remove the underlying operational fragmentation -- tax, employment law, and team management remain jurisdiction-specific (European Business Review)
  • ❌ Several EU member states impose capital gains tax when a founder relocates their company to another EU country, a friction EU Inc. would not automatically resolve (Börsen-Zeitung)

Radar

  • 🧑 McDermott Will & Emery and Orrick both publish substantive EU Inc. briefings this cycle -- signals the major transatlantic law firm tier is now actively advising clients on the proposal.
